standardPageLoadTime.description:
The legacy way of measuring page load time: the duration between the timestamp of the
`PerformanceTiming.navigationStart` event and the timestamp of the `PerformanceTiming.loadEventEnd` event.

Reference:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformanceTiming/navigationStart
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformanceTiming/loadEventEnd

ajaxRequestLoadTime.description:
Page load time based on network requests: the duration between the timestamp of the
`PerformanceTiming.navigationStart` event and the timestamp when all ajax requests finished.

Reference:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformanceTiming/navigationStart

timeToInteractive.description:
How long it takes a page to become interactive.
"Interactive" is defined as the point where:
- The page has displayed useful content, which is measured with First Contentful Paint. The "first-contentful-paint"
  is tracked by PerformancePaintTiming (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformancePaintTiming)
- There is no long task (more than 50 milliseconds) running at the moment over a period of 5 seconds. The page responds
  to user interactions within 50 milliseconds.
  All long tasks are recorded by PerformanceObserver API. (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Long_Tasks_API)
  When an iteration of the polling loop (setInterval) runs, it means the main thread is not blocked by a long task.
- There is no AJAX request over a period of 5 seconds.

The latest timestamp of a valid quiet period (defined by no long running task and no network request within a 5 second period)
is used as the end of the timeToInteractive while performance.timing.navigationStart is used as the start.

Reference:
https://web.dev/articles/tti

timeToInteractiveLegacy.description:
How long it takes a page to become interactive (legacy definition).
"Interactive" is defined as the point where:
- The page has displayed useful content, which is measured with First Contentful Paint. The "first-contentful-paint"
  is tracked by PerformancePaintTiming (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformancePaintTiming)
- There is no long task (more than 50 milliseconds) running at the moment. The page responds
  to user interactions within 50 milliseconds.
  All long tasks are recorded by PerformanceObserver API. (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Long_Tasks_API)
  When an iteration of the polling loop (setInterval) runs, it means the main thread is not blocked by a long task.

The latest timestamp among the last long task, first contentful paint and performance.timing.loadEventEnd is used as the
end of the timeToInteractive while performance.timing.navigationStart is used as the start.

Reference:
https://developers.google.com/web/tools/lighthouse/audits/time-to-interactive
https://github.com/WICG/time-to-interactive#definition
https://web.dev/interactive
